why: The PE draw the tower 17% and the south wing 15% narrower than the cadastre measures them; the north wing and the gaps between are right. Each pair is one wall: where the plans put the rooms against it, then where the rooms go, a wall's thickness (10 units, 0.3 m) inside the cadastre's face. The walls are the Calle 63 facade (P2's library), the tower's west face (P3-P5), its east face (P1-P5), the south wing's west face (P3-P5, above the auditorium) and the Calle 62 facade (P5-P8). Mapped so, P1's rooms along the Calle 63 stand a wall inside the sidewalk that runs under the north wing.

groups.why: The PE draw the auditorium shallower than the south wing it fills. Its back, on the lot next door, goes a wall inside the wing's; its front stops short of the wing's stepped front on the Carrera 9 Bis, leaving the foyer its own plan draws there.

limits.why: Brian: the central wing is roofed out to the Carrera 9A, though the cadastre records no part there. The hall runs to a wall inside the lot's edge.
Its east wall is the tower's: past it is the open passage beside the Casa de Francisco de Paula Velez.
The ramp stays inside the lot, a wall short of the Carrera 9A sidewalk.
The lobby ends a wall short of the open passage.
A wall inside the Calle 62 facade.
A wall inside the Calle 62 facade.
Past the auditorium's west wall the cadastre leaves a gap between the south wing's parts, open to the passage.

corridors.name: Pasillo transversal
corridors.why: The PE's route from the exit on the Calle 63, under the north stair and the central lifts and stairs, to the auditorium's lobby.

corridors.name: Paso a la salida de la Carrera 9A
corridors.why: The PE's route down the open passage beside the Casa de Francisco de Paula Velez to the exit on the Carrera 9A.

corridors.name: Paso por el salon central
corridors.why: The PE's route across the central hall, out to the passage.

place.why: The plan draws the tower's floor against the Calle 63 side of the building, where the north wing stands up to P5. Moved as a whole so its lifts and stairs stack on P3-P5's.

P6.why: Brian: on P6 the south wing is the south terrace and a couple of offices; the plan paints the whole wing, and that shape is the terrace.
